mainTopic: בלעם's empty boast, ה׳'s daily moment of anger, and how בלעם's blessings hid curses
overview: This amud is all about בלעם and the people around his story. בלעם boasted that he 'knows the knowledge of the Most High,' but the גמרא shows he could not even out-argue his own donkey. So the boast is explained differently: he only knew how to pinpoint the one short moment each day when ה׳ is angry. The sign of that moment is a rooster's comb that turns fully white. ה׳ held back His anger in בלעם's days, so the curses failed. רבי יהושע בן לוי tried to use that moment to curse a heretic, fell asleep, and learned that a צדיק should not curse anyone. The גמרא then teaches that love and hatred both make a great person drop his dignity, as with אברהם and בלעם. It also teaches that doing מצוות שלא לשמה leads to לשמה, since בלק's קרבנות earned him the descendant רות. This leads to a side discussion about wishing that a son or student be greater than oneself. Finally, רבי יוחנן shows that each of בלעם's blessings hid a curse, and רבי אבא בר כהנא says all of those curses later came true except the one about בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות. The amud ends by beginning to explain why the curse of אחיה השילוני was better than בלעם's blessing, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the verse about סיסרא and יעל
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the פסוק from שופטים 5:27, which finishes the earlier proof about סיסרא and יעל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He sank, he fell, he lay, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a פסוק it began on the previous page. This line closes the earlier discussion about סיסרא and יעל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full פסוק describes סיסרא at יעל's feet. On the previous page, the גמרא read its repeated verbs as a proof about what happened between them. Here we only see the tail end, so nothing new is argued in this line.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And so on.' The rest of the פסוק continues

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the previous topic about סיסרא and יעל. The new topic about בלעם starts in the next step.

phrases.english: "He sank, he fell, he lay, etc."
phrases.notes: שופטים 5:27. The quote began on the previous page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous page's discussion about סיסרא and יעל.
steps.raayaObject: The earlier claim about סיסרא and יעל

steps.title: How could בלעם know God's mind if he didn't know his donkey's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בלעם's boast that he 'knows the knowledge of the Most High.' It challenges it: he did not even understand his own animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he knows the knowledge of the Most High.' Now, he did not even know the mind of his own animal, and he knew the mind of the Most High?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes בלעם describing himself as someone who knows God's mind, and asks how that can be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge uses simple logic: someone who cannot understand a donkey surely cannot understand God. The challenge already assumes that בלעם failed to understand his animal. The next step explains what that failure was.

keyTerms.meaning: The knowledge (mind) of the Most High, meaning God
'Now.' Used here to mean 'if even this is so, how could that be?'

phrases.english: "And he knows the knowledge of the Most High."
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:16. בלעם is describing himself.

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא דַּעַת בְּהֶמְתּוֹ לָא הֲוָה יָדַע,
phrases.english: Now, the mind of his animal he did not know,
and the mind of the Most High he knew?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דַּעַת בְּהֶמְתּוֹ לָא הֲוָה יָדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about בלעם, unrelated to סיסרא.
steps.kashyaTarget: בלעם's claim in the פסוק that he knows God's mind
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he could not understand even his own donkey, he surely could not understand the Most High.

steps.title: The princes ask why בלעם is riding a donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what 'the mind of his animal' refers to. The princes asked בלעם why he was not riding horses, and he made an excuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'the mind of his animal'? The princes said to him: Why aren't you riding horses? He said to them: I sent them out to the pasture.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the story behind 'he didn't know his animal's mind.' It sets up the conversation with the donkey that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Riding a donkey looked undignified for an important prophet, so the princes asked about it. בלעם covered up with an excuse: his horses were resting in the pasture. The donkey will soon expose this excuse.

phrases.english: What is "the mind of his animal"?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרִי לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא רָכְבַתְּ סוּסְיָא?
phrases.english: That they said to him: Why didn't you ride horses?
phrases.notes: 'They' are the princes of מואב traveling with בלעם.

phrases.english: He said to them: I sent them out to the pasture.
phrases.notes: Literally, 'I threw them into the moist place,' meaning green grazing land where they can rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the assumption behind the challenge in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What event shows that בלעם did not know his animal's mind?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The princes asked why he rode a donkey, and he gave a false excuse about his horses being out to pasture.

steps.title: The donkey knocks down בלעם's excuses
steps.stepSummary: Reading במדבר 22:30 as a debate, the donkey answers each of בלעם's excuses with words from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The donkey said to him: 'Am I not your donkey?' He answered: Just for carrying loads. She said: 'That you have ridden upon.' He answered: Only by chance. She said: 'Ever since you existed until this day!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the donkey's words in the פסוק as a back-and-forth argument. The donkey refutes each excuse בלעם gives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק answers an excuse. 'Your donkey' shows she belongs to him. When he says she is only for loads, 'that you rode' answers that. When he says riding her was rare, 'all your life until today' shows he rode her regularly. בלעם is shown to be wrong in front of everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: The parts in quotation marks are the donkey quoting the פסוק. The short lines in between are בלעם's excuses, which the גמרא adds without saying 'he said.'

phrases.english: She said to him: "Am I not your donkey?"
phrases.notes: במדבר 22:30.

phrases.english: Merely for carrying loads.
phrases.notes: This is בלעם answering: you're my donkey, but not for riding.

phrases.english: "That you have ridden upon me!"
Merely by chance.
"Ever since you existed, until this day!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story, showing how בלעם's excuse fell apart.
steps.raayaObject: That בלעם did not understand, and could not outwit, his own donkey
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 22:30, read phrase by phrase as a debate

steps.title: The donkey's final point, learned from the word הַהַסְכֵּן
steps.stepSummary: The donkey adds that she serves בלעם even as a wife at night. The גמרא learns this through a גזירה שוה between הַהַסְכֵּן and the word סֹכֶנֶת used for אבישג.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but I also act as a wife for you at night. It is written here, 'Was I ever accustomed (הַהַסְכֵּן הִסְכַּנְתִּי),' and it is written there, 'And she will be a companion (סֹכֶנֶת) to him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The donkey makes her last and most shaming point against בלעם. The גמרא shows where this is hinted in the פסוק by comparing a shared word root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The root ס־כ־ן appears both in the donkey's words and in the description of אבישג, who was brought to be close to דוד המלך. Because the same root is used, the גמרא reads the donkey's word as hinting at a close, intimate relationship too. This completes the picture of how low בלעם was, the very man who claimed to know God's mind.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is written here... and it is written there.' The standard way of comparing words in two פסוקים (גזירה שוה)
A close companion; the word used for אבישג

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא turns בלעם's boast upside down. The man who said he knew God's mind could not understand or out-argue his own donkey, and the donkey exposed his private shame.
steps.whyThisMatters: This passage is part of the גמרא's larger picture of בלעם's bad character. It shows that his spiritual claims were empty.

phrases.english: And not only that, but I perform [for you]
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets belongs to the corrected wording.

phrases.english: marital relations at night.
It is written here: "Was I ever accustomed?"
phrases.notes: במדבר 22:30. Notice the root ס־כ־ן in these words.

phrases.english: And it is written there: "And she will be a companion to him."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:2, about אבישג and דוד המלך. Same root ס־כ־ן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the donkey's final, strongest point and gives its source.
steps.raayaObject: The donkey's claim of an intimate relationship with בלעם
steps.raayaSupportSource: גזירה שוה from the root ס־כ־ן: במדבר 22:30 and מלכים א 1:2

steps.title: What בלעם really knew: the moment of anger
steps.stepSummary: Since בלעם could not really know הקדוש ברוך הוא's mind, the גמרא explains the פסוק: he knew how to pinpoint the moment when הקדוש ברוך הוא is angry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'and he knows the knowledge of the Most High' mean? That he knew how to pinpoint the exact moment in which הקדוש ברוך הוא is angry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just shown that בלעם was not so wise, so it now explains what the boast 'he knows the knowledge of the Most High' really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא from step 2 was that someone who did not understand his own donkey cannot know הקדוש ברוך הוא's mind. The answer narrows the boast: בלעם did not know הקדוש ברוך הוא's thoughts. He only knew the timing of one short daily moment of anger, and he cursed at that moment.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowledge of the Most High, meaning הקדוש ברוך הוא
To aim at or pinpoint exactly

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'and he knows the knowledge of the Most High' mean?
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:16. 'Rather' means: since he clearly did not know הקדוש ברוך הוא's mind, what is the פסוק really saying?

phrases.english: That he knew how to pinpoint that moment
in which the Holy One, Blessed be He, is angry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the קשיא of step 2 and gives the real meaning of בלעם's boast.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בלעם knew הקדוש ברוך הוא's actual thoughts
steps.terutzMaskana: בלעם only knew the timing of הקדוש ברוך הוא's daily moment of anger

steps.title: The prophet מיכה‎: ה׳ held back His anger in בלעם's days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the idea from a פסוק in מיכה‎: ה׳'s 'righteous acts' were that He did not get angry at all during בלעם's days, so the curse could not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the prophet told ישראל: 'My people, remember what בלק advised and what בלעם answered... so that you may know ה׳'s righteous acts.' What are those righteous acts? הקדוש ברוך הוא said: Know how many kindnesses I did for you, that I did not get angry during all the days of בלעם. If I had gotten angry, nothing would have been left of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from מיכה that fits the idea that בלעם's power depended on a moment of anger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'righteous acts of ה׳' is explained as a specific kindness: הקדוש ברוך הוא did not become angry at all during those days. If בלעם's power was cursing at the moment of anger, then holding back that anger made his whole plan useless.

keyTerms.meaning: The righteous acts or kindnesses of ה׳
If not for, had it been that
A survivor or escapee; anyone left at all

phrases.english: And this is what the prophet said to Israel:

phrases.aramaic: ״עַמִּי זְכָר נָא מַה יָּעַץ בָּלָק מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב
phrases.english: 'My people, remember now what Balak, king of Moab, advised,'
phrases.notes: מיכה 6:5

phrases.aramaic: וּמֶה עָנָה אֹתוֹ בִּלְעָם בֶּן בְּעוֹר
phrases.english: and what Balaam, son of Beor, answered him,
from Shittim to Gilgal,
so that you may know the righteous acts of ה׳.'
What does 'so that you may know the righteous acts of ה׳' mean?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel:

phrases.aramaic: דְּעוּ נָא כַּמָּה צְדָקוֹת עָשִׂיתִי עִמָּכֶם,
phrases.english: Know how many kindnesses I did with you,
that I did not become angry all those days,
in the days of Balaam the wicked,
for had I become angry all those days,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר מִשּׂוֹנְאֵיהֶן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׂרִיד וּפָלִיט.
phrases.english: not a single survivor would have remained of the enemies of Israel.
phrases.notes: 'Enemies of Israel' is a polite way of saying Israel itself, so the גמרא doesn't say something bad about ישראל directly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 6 by showing a פסוק that fits the idea that בלעם's power depended on הקדוש ברוך הוא's anger.
steps.raayaObject: That הקדוש ברוך הוא held back His anger during בלעם's days so the curse could not work
steps.raayaSupportSource: מיכה 6:5, 'so that you may know the righteous acts of ה׳'

steps.title: בלעם himself admits ה׳ was not angry
steps.stepSummary: בלעם's own words to בלק, 'How can I curse whom God has not cursed,' show that ה׳ was not angry in those days.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what בלעם told בלק: 'How can I curse, whom God has not cursed?' During those days ה׳ was not angry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second support, this time from בלעם's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלעם admits that he cannot curse, because ה׳ has not 'cursed' or been angry. This fits step 7: with no moment of anger to use, בלעם's special skill did nothing.

phrases.english: That is what Balaam said to Balak:
'How can I curse, whom God has not cursed, etc.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 23:8

phrases.english: (During those days ה׳ was not angry.)
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't. The square brackets give the corrected word: 'days' instead of 'day'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second proof for the same point as step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳ was not angry during בלעם's days
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 23:8, 'How can I curse, whom God has not cursed'

steps.title: ה׳'s anger comes daily but lasts only a moment
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ is angry every day, but only for a single moment, as the פסוק says, 'His anger is for a moment.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'God is angry every day.' And how long is His anger? A moment, as it says: 'For His anger is for a moment, His favor is for a lifetime.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how long ה׳'s daily anger lasts, which shows how exact בלעם's timing had to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says ה׳ is angry every day. A second פסוק adds that this anger lasts only a moment. So בלעם's skill was knowing exactly when that tiny moment came.

keyTerms.meaning: A moment, a tiny unit of time

phrases.english: 'God is angry every day,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 7:12

phrases.english: and how long is His anger? A moment,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי רֶגַע בְּאַפּוֹ חַיִּים בִּרְצוֹנוֹ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it is said: 'For His anger is for a moment, life is in His favor, etc.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 30:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives more detail about the moment of anger that בלעם knew how to find.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long ה׳'s daily anger lasts

steps.title: Another פסוק for the moment of anger
steps.stepSummary: A second source from ישעיה shows that the anger lasts only a moment: 'Hide for a brief moment until the anger passes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, bring a different proof: 'Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your doors behind you; hide for a brief moment until the anger passes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another פסוק to prove the same point, that ה׳'s anger is only a moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of the פסוק in תהלים, the גמרא can use ישעיה. There the people only need to hide 'for a brief moment' until the anger passes, so the anger itself must be that short.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; brings another source or explanation

phrases.english: If you want, say: 'Go, my people, enter your rooms,'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 26:20

phrases.english: and shut your doors behind you;

phrases.aramaic: חֲבִי כִמְעַט רֶגַע עַד יַעֲבׇר זָעַם״.
phrases.english: hide for a brief moment until the anger passes.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different proof for the same point as step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳'s anger lasts only a moment

steps.title: When the anger comes: the rooster's white comb
steps.stepSummary: ה׳'s moment of anger falls in the first three hours of the day, at the time the rooster's comb turns white.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is He angry? In the first three hours of the day, when the rooster's comb turns white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks when during the day that moment of anger comes, and gives a sign to recognize it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the anger lasts a moment is not enough. One must also know when it comes. The גמרא places it in the first three hours of the day and gives a sign: the rooster's comb turns white.

keyTerms.meaning: The rooster's comb, the red crest on its head

phrases.english: When is He angry?
In the first three hours of the day,
when the rooster's comb turns white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting how long the anger lasts, this step sets when it comes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: At what time the moment of anger comes
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the first three hours, when the rooster's comb turns white

steps.title: But the comb turns white every hour
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the sign: the rooster's comb turns white at other hours too, so it cannot mark the special moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But every hour the comb also turns white!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the sign it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sign only helps if it appears at that moment and no other time. If the comb turns white every hour, it cannot show the one moment of anger.

phrases.english: Every single hour it also turns white!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the sign given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sign of the rooster's white comb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comb turns white at other hours too, so the sign does not single out the moment of anger

steps.title: The difference: red streaks
steps.stepSummary: At other hours the white comb still has red streaks. At the moment of anger it has no red streaks at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every other hour there are red streaks in it. At that moment there are no red streaks in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by making the sign more exact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comb does turn white at other hours, but red streaks remain. Only at the moment of anger is it completely white. So the sign still works.
steps.whatToRemember: בלעם's 'knowledge of the Most High' was only knowing the tiny daily moment of ה׳'s anger. ה׳ held back that anger in בלעם's days as a kindness to ישראל, so his curses failed.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שַׁעְתָּא וְשַׁעְתָּא אִית בֵּיהּ סוּרְיָקֵי סוּמָּקֵי,
phrases.english: Every other hour there are red streaks in it,

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא שַׁעְתָּא לֵית בֵּיהּ סוּרְיָקֵי סוּמָּקֵי.
phrases.english: but at that moment there are no red streaks in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שַׁעְתָּא וְשַׁעְתָּא אִית בֵּיהּ סוּרְיָקֵי סוּמָּקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by making the sign more exact.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any white comb marks the moment of anger, so the sign would show up every hour
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a fully white comb, with no red streaks, marks the moment of anger

steps.title: The heretic, the rooster, and the plan to curse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי tied up a rooster to catch ה׳'s moment of anger so he could curse a heretic neighbor, but when the moment came he dozed off.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heretic lived near רבי יהושע בן לוי and kept bothering him. One day רבי יהושע בן לוי took a rooster, tied it by its leg, and sat and watched it. He said: 'When that moment comes, I will curse him.' When the moment came, he fell asleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that puts the rooster sign from the last steps to use. רבי יהושע בן לוי tries to use ה׳'s moment of anger to curse someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11-13 taught that the moment of anger can be spotted when the rooster's comb turns fully white. Here someone actually tries to use that sign. The story ends with a surprise: he falls asleep exactly at that moment, and the next step explains what he learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic, someone who denies the Torah

phrases.english: There was a certain heretic who lived in the neighborhood
of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
who would keep upsetting him.
One day he took a rooster,
tied it by its leg, and sat and watched.
phrases.notes: He's watching for the comb to turn completely white, the sign from steps 11-13.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: כִּי מְטָא הָהוּא שַׁעְתָּא – אֶילְטְיֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He said: When that moment arrives, I will curse him.
When that moment arrived, he dozed off.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִינָא דַּהֲוָה בְּשִׁיבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rooster sign from steps 11-13 in a real-life story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story: an attempt to use ה׳'s moment of anger to curse a heretic was blocked when רבי יהושע בן לוי fell asleep.

steps.title: Cursing even a heretic is not proper
steps.stepSummary: From falling asleep, רבי יהושע בן לוי concluded that it is not proper to punish others through curses, based on a פסוק in משלי, even when they are heretics.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Learn from this that it is not proper conduct, as it is written, 'Punishing, even for the righteous, is not good.' Even about heretics, a person should not say such a thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי draws the lesson from his story. Falling asleep showed him that he should not have tried to curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק as saying that a צדיק should not be the cause of someone else's punishment. The words 'even regarding heretics' push the lesson as far as it goes: even someone who truly bothers you should not be cursed by a righteous person.

keyTerms.meaning: Proper conduct, the right way to behave

steps.whatToRemember: Even though ה׳ has a daily moment of anger, a צדיק should not use it to curse anyone, not even a heretic.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא,
phrases.english: He said: Learn from this that it is not proper conduct,
as it is written: “Punishing, even for the righteous, is not good.”
phrases.notes: משלי 17:26

phrases.english: Even regarding heretics,
one should not say this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the moral lesson from the story in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is not proper for a צדיק to bring punishment on others through a curse, even on heretics.

steps.title: What triggers ה׳'s anger each morning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי מאיר explains that ה׳ becomes angry when the sun rises and kings put on their crowns and bow to the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי מאיר: When the sun rises, and the kings put their crowns on their heads and bow down to the sun, right away ה׳ becomes angry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains why ה׳'s moment of anger comes in the early morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the moment of anger falls in the first three hours of the day. Here we learn the reason: at sunrise the kings bow to the sun, which is עבודה זרה. Since that happens every morning, the anger comes every morning.

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir:
At the time when the sun rises,
and the kings place their crowns on their heads
and bow down to the sun, immediately He becomes angry.
phrases.notes: “He” means ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the topic of ה׳'s moment of anger and gives the reason it falls in the early morning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s daily anger is triggered when kings crown themselves at sunrise and bow to the sun.

steps.title: Love and hatred both break a great person's normal conduct
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק of בלעם saddling his own donkey, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that love (as with אברהם) and hatred (as with בלעם) both make a great person drop his usual dignified ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And בלעם rose in the morning and saddled his donkey.' It was taught in the name of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: Love cancels the normal conduct of a great person. We learn this from אברהם, as it is written, 'And אברהם rose early in the morning.' Hatred cancels the normal conduct of a great person. We learn this from בלעם, as it says, 'And בלעם rose in the morning and saddled his donkey.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of בלעם and explains a פסוק about him. It compares בלעם saddling his own donkey with אברהם doing the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great person normally has servants saddle his animal. אברהם did it himself out of love, because he was eager to do ה׳'s command. בלעם did it himself out of hatred, because he was eager to curse the Jewish people. Strong feelings, good or bad, make a person skip his usual dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: The normal conduct of a great, important person

steps.confusionAlert: Only the בלעם פסוק is quoted with the words 'and saddled his donkey.' The אברהם פסוק also continues with those same words, and that shared detail is the whole point of the comparison.

phrases.english: “And Balaam rose in the morning and saddled his donkey.”
phrases.notes: במדבר 22:21

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar:
Love cancels the normal conduct of a great person.
phrases.notes: An important person normally has a servant saddle his animal for him.

phrases.english: We learn this from Abraham, as it is written: “And Abraham rose early in the morning.”
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:3. That פסוק goes on: “and saddled his donkey.”

phrases.aramaic: שִׂנְאָה מְבַטֶּלֶת שׁוּרָה שֶׁל גְּדוּלָּה מִבִּלְעָם,
phrases.english: Hatred cancels the normal conduct of a great person. We learn this from Balaam,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיָּקׇם בִּלְעָם בַּבֹּקֶר וַיַּחֲבֹשׁ אֶת אֲתֹנוֹ״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: “And Balaam rose in the morning and saddled his donkey.”

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: אַהֲבָה מְבַטֶּלֶת שׁוּרָה שֶׁל גְּדוּלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of ה׳'s anger and returns to explaining the פסוקים of the בלעם story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Strong love or strong hatred makes a great person abandon his usual dignified conduct, as seen with אברהם and בלעם.

steps.title: Do Torah and מצוות even שלא לשמה, as seen from בלק
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that a person should always do Torah and מצוות even for the wrong reasons, because that leads to doing them for the right reasons. The proof is בלק, whose 42 קרבנות earned him the descendant רות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person should always be busy with Torah and מצוות, even not for their own sake, because by doing them not for their own sake he will come to do them for their own sake. For as a reward for the 42 קרבנות that בלק offered, he merited that רות came from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב teaches a general rule about serving ה׳ and backs it up with an example from בלק in this same story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלק brought his קרבנות for a bad goal, to get בלעם to curse the Jewish people. Even so, he was rewarded with a great descendant, רות. If even an act done with such a bad aim earns reward, then doing מצוות שלא לשמה is worthwhile and leads somewhere good.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for its own sake, for some other motive
For its own sake, purely for the מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: מתוך שלא לשמה בא לשמה: doing מצוות even for the wrong reasons is valuable, because it leads to doing them for the right reasons, and even בלק was rewarded for his קרבנות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the best-known principles about motivation in serving ה׳, and it is quoted all over Torah literature.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A person should always engage in Torah and מצוות,
even not for their own sake,
because from doing them not for their own sake, he comes to do them for their own sake.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבִּשְׂכַר אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁתַּיִם קׇרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁהִקְרִיב בָּלָק,
phrases.english: For as a reward for the forty-two offerings that Balak brought,
he merited that Ruth descended from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק אָדָם בְּתוֹרָה וּבְמִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the בלעם and בלק story but teaches a new general principle, using בלק as the proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should do Torah and מצוות even שלא לשמה, since it leads to לשמה. Proof: בלק's 42 קרבנות earned him the descendant רות.

steps.title: How רות came from בלק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר הונא explains the family line: רות was the daughter of עגלון, who was the grandson of בלק, king of מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר הונא said: רות was the daughter of עגלון, and עגלון was the son of the son of בלק, king of מואב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the family line, showing exactly how רות descended from בלק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step said רות came from בלק but did not explain how. רבי יוסי בר הונא supplies the missing links: בלק, then his son, then his grandson עגלון, then עגלון's daughter רות. This backs up רב's proof.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Huna said:
Ruth was the daughter of Eglon,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל בָּלָק מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב הָיְתָה.
phrases.english: who was the son of the son of Balak, king of Moab.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר הוּנָא: רוּת בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל עֶגְלוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the family connection behind רב's statement that רות came from בלק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רות was the daughter of עגלון, the grandson of בלק.

steps.title: How could the servants wish that שלמה be greater than דוד?
steps.stepSummary: רבא points to the פסוק where דוד's servants wish that שלמה's name and throne be greater than דוד's, and asks whether it is proper to speak to a king that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רבה בר מרי: It is written, 'May God make the name of שלמה better than your name and make his throne greater than your throne.' Is it proper to speak to a king like that?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a difficulty with a פסוק in מלכים: דוד's servants seem to tell the king that his son will be greater than he is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you show respect to a king and do not tell him someone will outshine him. So the plain reading of the פסוק seems to describe disrespectful speech. רבא wants to know how to understand it.

keyTerms.meaning: Proper manners; the respectful way people behave

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rabba bar Mari:

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב ״יֵיטֵב אֱלֹהִים אֶת שֵׁם שְׁלֹמֹה מִשְּׁמֶךָ
phrases.english: It is written: 'May God make the name of Solomon better than your name'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:47. דוד's servants are speaking to דוד.

phrases.english: 'and make his throne greater than your throne.'
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets belongs to the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְמֵימְרָא לֵיהּ לְמַלְכָּא הָכִי?
phrases.english: Is it proper conduct to speak to a king in this way?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְמֵימְרָא לֵיהּ לְמַלְכָּא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Following the mention of רות, ancestor of דוד's line, the גמרא moves to a פסוק about דוד and שלמה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of מלכים א 1:47
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Telling a king that his son will be greater than him seems disrespectful, so how could the servants say it?

steps.title: The wish meant 'like your throne', not 'greater'
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי answers that the servants meant 'a throne like yours', not one bigger than yours.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The meaning is 'of the same kind as' your throne.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מרי answers רבא: the wish was for שלמה's throne to be similar to דוד's, not greater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter מ in מִכִּסְאֶךָ usually means 'more than'. רבה בר מרי reads it as מֵעֵין, 'of the kind of', so the wish is 'may his throne be like yours'. This removes the disrespect.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the same kind as; similar to

steps.confusionAlert: The word מִכִּסְאֶךָ can mean 'more than your throne' or 'from the kind of your throne'. The whole answer depends on reading the מ the second way.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is saying to him: 'of the nature of' your throne.
phrases.notes: So מִכִּסְאֶךָ means 'like your throne', not 'bigger than your throne'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's difficulty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The servants wished that שלמה's throne be greater than דוד's, which seems disrespectful.
steps.terutzMaskana: They wished that שלמה's throne be like דוד's.

steps.title: Proof from the blessing of יעל
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי proves his reading: יעל is blessed 'more than the women in the tent', meaning the אמהות, which must also mean 'like them', not 'above them'.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say this, what about 'Blessed above women is יעל, wife of חבר the Kenite; above the women in the tent she shall be blessed'? Who are the women in the tent? שרה, רבקה, רחל and לאה. Is it proper to say that? Rather, it means 'like them'. So too here, it means 'like your throne'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מרי brings another פסוק that must be read the same way, to show his answer is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about יעל seems to say she is blessed more than the אמהות, which would be improper to say. So that פסוק must mean 'like the אמהות'. Since the same word-form is read as מֵעֵין there, it can be read that way in the פסוק about שלמה too.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so
The women in the tent (here: the אמהות)

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
'Blessed above women shall be Jael,'
phrases.notes: שופטים 5:24.

phrases.english: 'the wife of Heber the Kenite;'
'above the women in the tent she shall be blessed.'
The women in the tent, who are they?
Sarah, Rebecca, Rachel, and Leah.
Is it proper conduct to say this?
Rather, it is saying 'of the nature of' them.
So too here, it is saying 'of the nature of' your throne.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 21 with a parallel פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: Reading מִ־ as מֵעֵין ('like') instead of 'more than'
steps.raayaSupportSource: שופטים 5:24, the blessing of יעל compared to the אמהות
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה בר מרי, both פסוקים mean 'like', not 'greater than', because it would be improper to place someone above the king or above the אמהות.

steps.title: רב יוסי בר חוני: no jealousy of a son, proven from שלמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב יוסי בר חוני disagrees: a person is jealous of everyone except his son and his student, and the son part comes from דוד and שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רב יוסי בר חוני, who said: A person is jealous of everyone except his son and his student. His son: from שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an opinion that argues with רבה בר מרי's answer: the servants really did wish for שלמה to be greater, and that was fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסי בר חוני holds that a father is happy when his son outdoes him, so there is nothing disrespectful in wishing it. He learns this from the פסוק of שלמה read in its plain way, 'greater than your throne'. That is exactly the reading רבה בר מרי avoided.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for his son and his student

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Yosei bar Ḥoni,
phrases.notes: He disagrees with רבה בר מרי's 'like your throne' answer.

phrases.english: as Rav Yosei bar Ḥoni said:
A person is jealous of everyone,
except for his son and his student.
His son: we learn from Solomon,
phrases.notes: From the servants' wish that שלמה be greater than דוד, read the plain way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opinion that disagrees with the answer of steps 21-22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is jealous of everyone except his son and his student; the son part is learned from שלמה being wished greater than דוד.

steps.title: No jealousy of a student: from אלישע or from משה
steps.stepSummary: For the student, the גמרא gives two possible sources: אלישע asking for a double portion of אליהו's spirit, or משה leaning his hands on יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his student: if you want, say from 'Let there be a double portion of your spirit upon me'; and if you want, say from 'And he laid his hands upon him and commanded him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב יוסי בר חוני's teaching by showing where we learn that a teacher is not jealous of his student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע asked to be greater than his teacher אליהו, and that was accepted, so a teacher does not mind. The second source is משה leaning his hands (plural) on יהושע, showing generosity toward his student. Either פסוק works, so the גמרא offers both.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces another option)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on the servants' wish: רבה בר מרי says it meant 'like your throne'; רב יוסי בר חוני says it truly meant 'greater', since a father is not jealous of his son.

phrases.english: And his student: if you wish, say:
'Please let there be a double portion of your spirit upon me,'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 2:9. אלישע is asking his teacher אליהו.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
'And he laid his hands upon him and commanded him.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:23. משה with יהושע; notice the word 'hands', plural.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the sources for רב יוסי בר חוני's rule.
steps.raayaObject: A teacher is not jealous of his student
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 2:9 (אלישע) or במדבר 27:23 (משה and יהושע)

steps.title: What ה׳ put in בלעם's mouth: an angel or a hook
steps.stepSummary: Back to בלעם: on the פסוק 'And He placed a word in בלעם's mouth', רבי אלעזר says it was a מלאך and רבי יונתן says it was a hook.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And He placed a word in בלעם's mouth': רבי אלעזר says it was an angel; רבי יונתן says it was a hook.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the story of בלעם and brings a מחלוקת about what 'placing a word in his mouth' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that בלעם did not speak freely. רבי אלעזר says a מלאך spoke through him. רבי יונתן says ה׳ put something like a fish hook in his mouth to hold back anything else he wanted to say.

phrases.english: 'And He placed a word in Balaam's mouth,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 23:5.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: an angel,
Rabbi Yonatan says: a hook.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about דוד and שלמה, the גמרא returns to explaining the פסוקים about בלעם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ controlled בלעם's speech: according to רבי אלעזר through a מלאך, according to רבי יונתן through a hook in his mouth.

steps.title: בלעם's blessings show the curses he wanted to say
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that each phrase of בלעם's blessing reveals the curse he planned, starting with the tents, the שכינה, the kingdom, the fields, and the fragrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: From the blessing of that wicked man you can learn what was in his heart. He wanted to say they should have no בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות, and it came out 'How good are your tents, יעקב.' He wanted to say the שכינה should not rest on them, and it came out 'and your dwellings, ישראל.' He wanted to say their kingdom should not last, and it came out 'like streams stretched out.' He wanted to say they should have no olive trees and vineyards, and it came out 'like gardens by a river.' He wanted to say their fragrance should not spread, and it came out 'like aloes that ה׳ planted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's teaching that each blessing בלעם said was the reverse of a curse he had planned. He walks through the פסוקים one phrase at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the previous step, where הקב״ה put a word in בלעם's mouth. Each pair has two parts: first the curse בלעם wanted, then the פסוק that came out instead. So the blessing works like a mirror showing what was in his heart.
steps.confusionAlert: The first half of each pair is NOT what בלעם said out loud. It is what he wanted to say. The פסוק is what actually came out of his mouth.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
From the blessing of that wicked man
you can learn what was in his heart.
He wanted to say that they should not have
synagogues and study halls,
and instead it came out: "How good are your tents, Jacob."
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:5. In each pair, the first part is the curse he planned, and the פסוק is the blessing that came out instead.

phrases.english: He wanted to say that the Divine Presence should not rest on them,
and it came out: "and your dwellings, Israel."
phrases.notes: The word for dwellings, מִשְׁכְּנֹת, comes from the same root as שכינה.

phrases.english: He wanted to say that their kingdom should not last,
and it came out: "like streams stretched out."
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:6

phrases.english: He wanted to say that they should not have olive trees and vineyards,
and it came out: "like gardens by a river."
He wanted to say that their fragrance should not spread,
and it came out: "like aloes that ה׳ planted."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִבִּרְכָתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע אַתָּה לָמֵד מָה הָיָה בְּלִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the בלעם discussion: after learning that הקב״ה controlled his words, we see which curses were turned into blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each phrase of בלעם's blessing is the reverse of a curse he intended to say.

steps.title: The kingship curses turned into blessings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן continues his list with five curses about ישראל's kings and kingdom, each turned into a blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He wanted to say they should have no tall, impressive kings, and it came out 'like cedars by the water.' He wanted to say they should have no king son of a king, and it came out 'water will flow from his buckets.' He wanted to say their kingdom should not rule over the nations, and it came out 'and his seed in many waters.' He wanted to say their kingdom should not be strong, and it came out 'his king will be higher than אגג.' He wanted to say there should be no fear of their kingdom, and it came out 'and his kingdom will be raised high.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going with רבי יוחנן's same list. This part is all about kings and the kingdom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as before: planned curse, then the פסוק that came out instead. These pairs focus on royal height, kings passing the crown to sons, rule over nations, strength, and being feared.

keyTerms.meaning: People of height, impressive in stature
A king who is the son of a king

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִהְיוּ לָהֶם מְלָכִים בַּעֲלֵי קוֹמָה –
phrases.english: He wanted to say that they should not have tall, impressive kings,
and it came out: "like cedars by the water."

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִהְיֶה לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ בֶּן מֶלֶךְ –
phrases.english: He wanted to say that they should not have a king who is the son of a king,
and it came out: "water will flow from his buckets."
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:7. The water flowing on is read here as one king coming from another.

phrases.english: He wanted to say that their kingdom should not rule over the nations,
and it came out: "and his seed will be in many waters."
He wanted to say that their kingdom should not be strong,
and it came out: "and his king will be higher than Agag."
He wanted to say that there should be no fear of their kingdom,
and it came out: "and his kingdom will be raised high."

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יִהְיוּ לָהֶם מְלָכִים בַּעֲלֵי קוֹמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Direct continuation of רבי יוחנן's list from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blessings about ישראל's kings and kingdom are also reversed curses.

steps.title: All the curses came back except shuls and study halls
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא says that in the end all of בלעם's hidden curses came true, except the one about בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא says: All of them went back to being a curse, except for synagogues and study halls.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא adds a sad twist to רבי יוחנן's list: the blessings did not stay blessings forever. The next step gives his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן showed that the curses were turned into blessings. רבי אבא בר כהנא adds that this change was only temporary for most of them, and the hidden curses eventually came true. Only the curse against בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות stayed a blessing for good.

keyTerms.meaning: Went back to being a curse

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות are the one blessing of בלעם that was never taken away from ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana says:
All of them went back to being a curse,
phrases.notes: The curses בלעם secretly wanted ended up happening after all.

phrases.english: except for synagogues and study halls,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new idea on top of רבי יוחנן's list: most of the reversals were not permanent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the hidden curses eventually came true, except the one against בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.

steps.title: Proof from 'the curse' in the singular
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא proves his point from the פסוק that says ה׳ turned 'the curse' (singular) into a blessing, meaning only one curse was changed for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And ה׳ your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because ה׳ your God loved you.' It says 'curse', not 'curses'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רבי אבא בר כהנא's claim. He reads closely into one word of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses קללה, a single curse, and not קללות, many curses. So only one curse was turned into a blessing permanently. רבי אבא בר כהנא has already said which one stayed: the one about בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.

keyTerms.meaning: A curse, not curses (singular, not plural)

steps.whatToRemember: בלעם's blessings hid curses (רבי יוחנן). Most of those curses later came true, but the blessing on בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות stayed forever, because the פסוק says 'curse' in the singular (רבי אבא בר כהנא).

phrases.english: as it says:
"And ה׳ your God turned for you
the curse into a blessing
because ה׳ your God loved you."
phrases.notes: דברים 23:6

phrases.english: "Curse", and not "curses".

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיַּהֲפֹךְ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְּךָ אֶת הַקְּלָלָה לִבְרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי אבא בר כהנא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That only one of בלעם's curses was turned into a lasting blessing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 23:6, which uses the singular קללה instead of the plural קללות.

steps.title: A friend's curse is better than an enemy's blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן explains a פסוק in משלי: the curse of אחיה השילוני was better for ישראל than the blessing of בלעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says in the name of רבי יונתן: What does the פסוק mean, 'Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are too many'? The curse that אחיה השילוני cursed ישראל is better than the blessing that בלעם the wicked blessed them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that compares two speakers: a נביא who loved ישראל and cursed them, and בלעם who hated them and blessed them. The next step shows why the curse was better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a friend's 'wounds' are trustworthy, while an enemy's 'kisses' are not. רבי יונתן applies this: אחיה השילוני is the friend, so even his curse helps; בלעם is the enemy, so even his blessing hides harm. This fits with the previous steps, where בלעם's blessings hid curses that later came true.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani says
that Rabbi Yonatan says:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Faithful are the wounds of a friend,
but the kisses of an enemy are too many"?
phrases.notes: משלי 27:6

phrases.english: Better is the curse that
Achiya HaShiloni cursed Israel
than the blessing with which they were blessed by
Bilaam the wicked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related teaching: after seeing that בלעם's blessings turned to curses, it contrasts them with a loving נביא's curse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The curse of אחיה השילוני was better for ישראל than the blessing of בלעם.

steps.title: אחיה cursed ישראל with a reed that stands by water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that אחיה's curse compared ישראל to a reed in water, and begins explaining the good hidden inside that image.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחיה השילוני cursed ישראל with a reed, as it says: 'And ה׳ will strike ישראל as a reed sways in the water.' Just as this reed stands in a place of water, and its stem...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving why אחיה's curse was better, by looking at the picture he used: a reed by the water. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reed sways back and forth, which sounds like a curse. But the גמרא points out that a reed stands where there is water, which keeps it alive. So even inside the curse there is a blessing, and the description of the reed's stem continues after this.

phrases.aramaic: אֲחִיָּה הַשִּׁילוֹנִי קִילֵּל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּקָנֶה,
phrases.english: Achiya HaShiloni cursed Israel with a reed,
as it says:
"And ה׳ will strike Israel
as a reed sways in the water, etc."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 14:15

phrases.aramaic: מָה קָנֶה זֶה עוֹמֵד בִּמְקוֹם מַיִם,
phrases.english: Just as this reed stands in a place of water,
and its stem...

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחִיָּה הַשִּׁילוֹנִי קִילֵּל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּקָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins backing up רבי יונתן's claim by showing what was good in אחיה's curse.
steps.raayaObject: That אחיה's curse was better than בלעם's blessing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 14:15, comparing ישראל to a reed in water, which stands near what keeps it alive.
